cards: Merneptah was the fourth king of the 19th Dynasty of Egypt, son and successor of Ramesses II.
r. c. 1213–1203 BCE · Ancient Near East
Fu Hao was a consort of the Shang king Wu Ding who also led armies in the field, as oracle-bone inscriptions record.
d. c. 1200 BCE · Central & East Asia
Suppiluliuma II was the last known king of the Hittite Empire, reigning from about 1207 BCE.
r. from c. 1207 BCE · Ancient Near East
Wu Ding was a king of the Shang dynasty who reigned for several decades in the thirteenth century BCE from the capital at Yinxu, near Anyang.
Kashtiliash IV was a Kassite king of Babylon in the thirteenth century BCE.
r. c. 1232–1225 BCE · Ancient Near East
Kurunta was a Hittite prince, son of Muwatalli II, who ruled the appanage kingdom of Tarhuntassa in southern Anatolia in the 13th century BCE.
Alaksandu was a king of Wilusa in north-western Anatolia in the early 13th century BCE, known from a treaty he made with the Hittite king Muwatalli II around 1280 BCE.
r. c. 1280 BCE · Ancient Near East
Tarkasnawa was a king of Mira, a western Anatolian vassal kingdom of the Hittites, in the late 13th century BCE.
late 13th century BCE · Ancient Near East
